bg-raised.note: Rows, dialogs, menu, and toast. Stays opaque even under vibrancy.

label-2.note: Carries most repeated meta text; held above 4.5:1.

label-3.note: Verified >=4.5:1 on raised card, recessed kept row, and chrome grounds.

accent-fill.note: Darker in dark mode: carries white text on a selected menu item, must clear 4.5:1 there.

danger.note: Held dark enough in light mode to clear 4.5:1 as text on the tinted not_responding row (composites danger-tint over bg).

caution.note: Amber, deliberately not sharing the danger channel — caution means 'notice', danger means 'wrong'.

caution-border.note: The chip has no fill; this border is its whole affordance, so it runs at higher alpha than other hairlines.

title.purpose: "Portside" in the title bar. The system's one letterspacing value (-0.01em).

body.purpose: Server/service labels, dialog body copy, general sentence-case text.

meta.purpose: Section titles, uptime, health word, project heading, dialog title.

data.purpose: Port numbers, nerd grid, telemetry footer, source-menu path — confined to measured/counted values only.

shadows.name: shadow-popover
shadows.purpose: The system's only shadow token (dark mode: 0 8px 28px rgba(0,0,0,0.55), 0 1px 3px rgba(0,0,0,0.4)). Used exclusively by the popover menu, the dialog, and the toast — nothing at rest in the row flow carries a shadow.

motion.name: control-transition
motion.purpose: Titlebar and icon button hover/press transitions.

motion.name: row-actions-reveal
motion.purpose: Reveals a row's action cluster on hover/focus-within, or pins it visible during a pending stop or expanded state. A visibility toggle, not a recede device — see the Recede-By-Element-Color Rule for why this is a distinct, permitted use of opacity.

motion.name: refresh-spin
motion.purpose: Refresh icon while a refresh is in flight. Suppressed under prefers-reduced-motion.

vibrancy.note: windowEffects 'popover' + macOSPrivateApi (Cargo feature macos-private-api) make the real Tauri window transparent over an NSVisualEffectView. body.tauri (set in main.js pre-paint when window.__TAURI__ exists) gates translucent grounds; a plain browser keeps the opaque fallback automatically. Rows (--bg-raised) stay opaque in both cases.
vibrancy.caveat: Both alpha values were tuned by eye against a screenshot, not the real compiled window, and are pending a pass against the actual material.

antiReference.description: A prior, fully built and shipped direction: paper flight-progress strips clipped to a controller's board, holder-edge Kind-color coding, a cocked/rotated 'not responding' strip, letterspaced monospace stamps, a beige paper surface.
antiReference.status: rejected by the user as ugly; replaced entirely by this native-macOS system

narrative.overview: Portside is a native macOS menu-bar panel, played straight. It borrows nothing from a designed metaphor — no board, no paper, no stamped tickets — and everything from the first-party Apple vocabulary: system type, system grays, hairline separators, quiet controls that only surface on hover, one accent color used sparingly. The craft bar is Apple's own Control Center, Things 3, and iStat Menus. The tool's ambition is to disappear into the task. Light and dark are both first-class renditions of the same system, not one inverted from the other. A prior direction, an 'ATC strip board' world (paper flight-progress strips, holder-edge color coding, cocked/rotated alarm strips, letterspaced monospace stamps, a beige paper surface), was fully built and then rejected by the user as ugly. It is the anti-reference for this system: no paper strips, no holder edges, no cocked rotation, no letterspaced stamps, no beige.
keyCharacteristics: Native materials only: system sans, system grays, hairline dividers, native-weight vibrancy — no invented surface metaphor.
One accent, used only for the pressed/selected state and the dialog's default action.
Controls are quiet by default and reveal on hover/focus — the Control Center habit.
Status is never color-alone: the health word always ships beside the dot.
Recede is per-element color, never container opacity.
Monospace is reserved for data (ports, pids, nerd grid, telemetry); system sans carries every name and every sentence.

rules.name: The Beige Is the Anti-Reference Rule
rules.body: The network badge is a transparent hairline chip on the row's own ground, never a tinted/filled amber patch — a filled badge was the panel's last surviving trace of the rejected strip-board world.

rules.name: The One Ground, Two Chrome Strips Rule
rules.body: Only --bg (the panel) and the title bar / telemetry chrome go translucent under vibrancy; --bg-raised (every row, dialog, menu, toast) stays opaque in both a plain browser and the real window.

rules.name: The Data-Only Mono Rule
rules.body: Monospace is reserved for port numbers, the nerd grid, telemetry, and the source-menu path. Everything else is system sans in sentence case; no letterspacing anywhere except the panel title's -0.01em.

rules.name: The Recede-By-Element-Color Rule
rules.body: A receding row is never dimmed with opacity on its container, because opacity composites the whole subtree and a child cannot opt back out. Only named elements (label-3 on controls and quiet meta) recede; the health word and network badge never do. This does not prohibit opacity as a hover/focus reveal device, which .row-actions uses legitimately.

rules.name: The Cancel-Is-Default Rule
rules.body: Every dialog confirms a stop, so Cancel sits rightmost with the accent-filled default styling and programmatic focus, while the destructive action sits to its left, bordered only — a deliberate safety-first inversion of the platform's usual confirm-on-the-right convention.

dos: Do ship the health word next to the dot always — color is never the only carrier of status.
Do recede a row by naming individual elements (--label-3), never by setting opacity on the row container (The Recede-By-Element-Color Rule).
Do keep .health's word and .badge-network at full strength under every recede state, in both modes.
Do render the network badge as a transparent hairline chip on the row's own ground, never a filled tint.
Do make Cancel the rightmost, accent-filled default button in every confirmation dialog, and the destructive action bordered and never rightmost (The Cancel-Is-Default Rule).
Do confine monospace to port numbers, the nerd grid, telemetry, and the source-menu path; everything else is system sans, sentence case.
Do author light and dark as two first-class renditions, both verified >=4.5:1 on their real composited grounds.
Do treat vibrancy alphas (currently 0.72 panel / 0.6 chrome) as provisional until checked against the real compiled window.
donts: Don't reintroduce anything from the rejected 'ATC strip board' world: no paper strips, no holder-edge color coding, no cocked/rotated alarm state, no letterspaced stamps, no beige.
Don't dim a receding row (or any subtree) with container opacity — it composites the whole subtree into one layer, so a child cannot opt back out.
Don't give a watch-only row a disabled Stop button as a stand-in for 'no action' — the layout has no action slot for that row kind at all.
Don't offer 'go to source' on a row whose project path is null, or on a watch-only row — both would either lie or point nowhere.
Don't letterspace or uppercase section titles or button labels; sentence case throughout, with the panel title's -0.01em as the system's one tracking value.
